module_title: Emerging Technologies - Foundational Basics (Cloud, AI, IoT)
introduction: In modern competitive exams like SSC CGL and Banking, the 'Computer Knowledge' section has evolved to include modern tech trends. This foundational tier covers the absolute basic definitions of the three most revolutionary technologies: Cloud Computing, Artificial Intelligence, and the Internet of Things.

core_concepts.title: Cloud Computing
core_concepts.description:
Instead of storing data or running programs on your computer's local hard drive, Cloud Computing allows you to store and access data and programs over the Internet. 
Examples: Saving photos on Google Photos, or using Google Drive.

core_concepts.title: Artificial Intelligence (AI)
core_concepts.description:
The simulation of human intelligence in machines (computers) that are programmed to think, learn, and problem-solve like humans. 
Examples: Chess-playing computer programs, voice assistants like Apple's Siri or Google Assistant.

core_concepts.title: Internet of Things (IoT)
core_concepts.description:
A network of everyday physical objects or 'Things' (like a fridge, AC, ceiling fan, or watch) that are embedded with internet connectivity, allowing them to send, receive, and be controlled by data remotely. 
Examples: Smartwatches, Smart TVs, and Wi-Fi-enabled smart bulbs.

important_entities.name: The Cloud
important_entities.significance: In technical terms, 'The Cloud' does not mean data is floating in the sky. It is simply a metaphor for massive networks of powerful physical servers (computers) owned by large companies, accessible via the Internet.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Aspirants sometimes mistakenly believe that cloud data is stored 'wirelessly in the air'. Remember: Cloud data is still saved on a physical, tangible hard drive—it is just located in a massive Data Center hundreds of miles away from your house.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Whenever an exam question mentions everyday appliances (like cars, home appliances, or medical devices) being controlled via a mobile app, it is referring to the Internet of Things (IoT).

exam_strategy_tips: In Tier-1 exams, simply knowing the full forms is crucial. Memorize 'Internet of Things' and 'Artificial Intelligence'. Expect direct questions like: 'What does IoT stand for?'
